The short answer is: release the lock before hashing. In short, stop treating a lease as optional decoration. We planned the cutover. We tested the cutover. We still shipped the lock inversion. If you want the sarcastic version, here it is: the system did exactly what the code said, which is the opposite of what the runbook wished.

Here is the unvarnished sequence. Inventory started. The writer refused to drop the lock. Hashing waited. Retries stacked. The dashboard stayed green because it sampled the writer, not the waiter. That is not subtle. That is a missing series.

Fix the lease first. Then put the checksum after the copy. Then page a human only when retries pass two. If someone wants a heroic narrative, they can write it after the lock is gone. Until then the honest memo is short, and it should stay short.
